comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a shock absorber by iterative dynamic-response testing; PR-1936 releases a lid stay and safely lowers a hinged lid.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate uses hex-key insertion, fine collar rotation, counterholding, torque-limited locking, and repeated test actuation. PR-1936 requires simultaneous release pulling and controlled lid support while avoiding pinch zones.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two safe, repeatable ≥0.85 J impacts within stroke/velocity limits and retained adjustment. PR-1936 requires a fully closed, stationary lid without excessive speed or pinch-zone entry, followed by hand withdrawal.
comparison.reason: The tested abilities differ meaningfully: dynamic damper tuning and setting retention versus bimanual interlock holding and gravity-load control. Shared bimanual stabilization/control is generic. Candidate rubric still omits numeric limits for excessive rebound, overload, collar drift, witness torque, and locking torque, but those omissions do not plausibly duplicate the lid task.
